name: Tuttle Creek State Park - South Randolph Area
note: South Randolph campground of Tuttle Creek State Park (KDWP), on a wooded rise above the east shore at the lake's north end, entered by Randolph Park Road off K-16 just east of the Randolph Bridge: two small gravel loops of electric sites, plus about 50 unreserved primitive sites. It is the park's horse-camping base (horse pens, wash racks, the Randolph equestrian trail) but sells ordinary RV and tent sites; water is from community hydrants, not at the sites. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: campitks.gov (2026-11-06): the 'South Randolph' loop (510335) on parkID 519132 lists 20 sites, 192-211, all 'Standard with Electric Hookup' 50/30/20 A, site-specific reservable, 'Looking For Category: RV Site,Tent Site,Trailer Site', gravel, 'Maximum Vehicle Length' 40-53 ft (12 at 50), 3 pull-through (193, 200, 201), plus a day-use group shelter; KDWP's South Randolph page (search snippet, 2026-11-06) gives 20 electric and 50 primitive sites with a community water hydrant system, horse pens, wash racks, a shower building and restroom. A separate place from 13952 Fancy Creek: South Randolph sits on the EAST side of Tuttle Creek Lake on its own road (OSM 'Randolph Park Road', tagged camp_site 'South Randolph Campground'), while Fancy Creek's loops are on the west bank, 2.4 km away across the water and the K-16 Randolph Bridge (Esri imagery 2026-11-06). Its 20 sites are not 13952's 24: campitks' 'Fancy Creek' loop (510655) is its own 24 sites, 168-191. General campground with horse facilities, not a horse-only camp (campitks sells the sites as RV/tent/trailer sites; a 2021 Dyrt reviewer of the Randolph unit tent-camped and found it 'predominantly RV campers'). Public campground, no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: Esri World Imagery with all 20 campitks site coordinates plotted (2026-11-06): both loops sit in a clearing on a wooded rise, about 250-300 m east of the Tuttle Creek Lake shore, with a continuous tree belt between them and the water; no site sees open water. campitks marks every site 'Proximity to Water: None' and gives no 'River/Lake View'. DEM (Open-Meteo) 370 m at the pin against 328 m on the lake just west, so the loops are ~40 m above the water on a bluff. Not near the dam (the dam is ~25 km south) -> not waterfront.

fees.note: KDWP's statewide schedule from November 1, 2026: a daily camping permit of $17.75 a night per camping unit, plus $11 a night for one utility (electric), so an electric site costs $28.75 and a primitive site $17.75. None of the South Randolph sites is a designated prime site. A $2.75 processing fee per stay and a vehicle permit ($7 a day) are charged on top. Read 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-06.

fees_source: https://ksoutdoors.gov/licenses-permits-fees/kansas-state-park-entrance-and-camping-fees (as stored on sibling 2115, read 2026-10-15: permit $17.75; utilities $11 / $13 / $15 for one / two / three; prime $2 April-September; $2.75 processing fee; $7 vehicle permit); fee shape copied from 2115 minus the water, full-hookup and prime surcharges this area lacks. campitks campsiteDetails for 192-211: 'Number of Utilities: 1' on 192-207 (2 on 208-211, see flags), no 'Prime Site', read 2026-11-06.

min_stay.season: Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule)

booking.note: The 20 electric sites reserve site-specific on Kansas's ReserveAmerica site (campitks.gov) or by calling the park office; self-registration on arrival is allowed. The ~50 primitive sites are not on the reservation site. The reservation window shown on 2026-11-06 ran from Nov 8, 2026 to Dec 6, 2027. 2027 holiday minimum: 3 nights over Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day weekends. Up to 14 consecutive nights in one campground, then move to another campground in the park.

booking_source: https://www.campitks.gov/camping/tuttle-creek-state-park/r/campgroundDetails.page?parkID=519132 ('2027 CAMPSITES Holiday Minimum Stay Rule: Memorial Day: 3 night minimum, Independence Day: 3 night minimum, Labor Day: 3 night minimum'; '14 days maximum consecutive stay rule'; 'Open year round.'), and campsiteDetails for siteID 3722-3741 ('Site Reserve Type: Site-Specific', 'Self Reg Allowed: Y', 'Reservation Window: Sun Nov 08 2026 - Mon Dec 06 2027'), read 2026-11-06

SEWER ODDITY, not stamped: campitks gives 'Sewer Hookup: Y' and 'Number of Utilities: 2' on 208-211 (4 of 20), with no water hookup and a site type of 'Standard with Electric Hookup'; KDWP's page counts all 20 as electric. Sewer-without-water looks like a data-entry slip (or a horse-area quirk), so I left sewer absent and the fee at one utility; AWH may want sewer true if the 4-site rule should apply.

sites: count 20 reservable electric (KDWP also lists ~50 primitive, not on campitks), max_rig_ft 53 (192 and 197; twelve at 50), pull_through true (193, 200, 201), surface gravel - campitks campsiteDetails 192-211, read 2026-11-06. (The brief's 'max 50 ft' was a slight undercount.)

facilities: showers true ('Shower House with Restrooms: Y' at all 20 sites; KDWP snippet 'shower building and restroom'), flush_toilets true ('Modern Restrooms: Within 1/4 Mile'), vault_toilets true ('Vault Toilet: Within 1/4 Mile') - campitks campsiteDetails, read 2026-11-06. Dump station NOT stamped: one search summary of KDWP's page lists one, Campendium shows none at the campground.

Horse camping: South Randolph is the park's equestrian base (horse pens, wash racks, Randolph equestrian trail; Back Country Horsemen installed pens on 'the 200 loop'). Judged a general campground with horse facilities, not a horse-only camp, because campitks sells every site as 'RV Site,Tent Site,Trailer Site' (it names equestrian loops elsewhere, e.g. Boulder Bluff's 'Equestrian Loop'), and a 2021 Dyrt reviewer camped in a tent among 'predominantly RV campers'. KDWP's own page returned 403 (ksoutdoors.gov) and the Wayback Machine blocked me, so KDWP's wording is cited from search snippets only - AWH may want to confirm that non-horse campers are welcome.

No correction needed to 13952's electric count: campitks' Fancy Creek loop (510655) is its own 24 electric sites, 168-191 (20 at 30/20 A, 4 at 50/30/20 A; 7 pull-through; 35-110 ft; gravel/asphalt), in two pods - 168-179 around 39.4405,-96.7385 and 180-191 around 39.4433,-96.7333 (13952's pin). The other loops near it hold no campsites: Fancy Creek Hidden Hollow (510658) = 9 shelters (29-37), N Randolph (510657) = 2 group shelters, Fancy Creek Lake View (510659) = empty.

Side finding for 13952 (not changed): campitks marks Fancy Creek 180-191 'River/Lake View: Y' (168-179 none), while 13952 is stored 'not waterfront' from a 2026-09-29 satellite look; its next phase 7 pass should re-run the gate on 180-191 for a possible lakeview.
